data.narrative:
Ursa Space Systems is a Series C-stage space and aerospace company that has raised approximately $67M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a universe of 6 same-sector and same/adjacent-stage private peers (including Sierra Space at $8.0B, Apex Space at $2.3B, and Varda Space Industries at $1.6B) alongside 5 public comparables in the Space & Aerospace sector.

Two quantitative methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $67M total raised and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, implies a valuation of $114M. Peer-median methodology across the 6-company private comp set yields $1.8B, reflecting the broad dispersion in the sector ($1.1B–$8.0B range). Public-comp anchoring using a 27.4x median price-to-sales multiple for sector peers cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures. These two methods triangulate to a valuation range of $97M (low) to $2.1B (high), with a median of $952M.

The wide midpoint reflects material uncertainty inherent to early-stage space ventures: peer valuations span nearly an order of magnitude, and the target's specific technology, customer traction, and capital efficiency relative to the comp set remain pivotal drivers. Revenue visibility, path to unit economics, and founder track record warrant scrutiny in narrowing this range.
